coreLogic: Self-contained inline expression, no sub-delegation: `return $this->flags && self::FLAG_ESCALATE;` (line 117). FLAG_ESCALATE is the class constant `const FLAG_ESCALATE = 0x0002` (line 28) on SLA. This is a pre-existing bug in the legacy code: it uses PHP's logical AND (&&) instead of bitwise AND (&). Because self::FLAG_ESCALATE (2) is itself always truthy as a scalar operand, `$this->flags && self::FLAG_ESCALATE` reduces to 'is $this->flags non-zero', NOT 'is the FLAG_ESCALATE bit set in $this->flags'. The SAME class has the correct pattern used elsewhere for identical bit-check purposes: SLA::hasFlag($flag) (line 101-103) does `($this->get('flags', 0) & $flag) != 0`, and SLA::getInfo() (lines 72-80) does `$base['enable_priority_escalation'] = $this->flags & self::FLAG_ESCALATE` (line 77, correct bitwise AND). $this->flags itself is a plain ORM-hydrated property (populated from the `flags` column on the underlying sla DB table when the row is loaded via SLA::lookup()/SLA::objects()) — priorityEscalation() does not read or write it via any accessor. Persistence of the FLAG_ESCALATE bit happens only in SLA::update() (lines 186-192): it rebuilds `$this->flags = ($vars['isactive'] ? FLAG_ACTIVE : 0) | $vars['disable_overdue_alerts'] | $vars['enable_priority_escalation'] | $vars['transient']`, where $vars['enable_priority_escalation'] is expected to already be either 0 or self::FLAG_ESCALATE (2) as posted from the SLA edit form in include/staff/slaplan.inc.php, then calls $this->save(). getInfo() and update() are adjacent/related flag-storage code, not part of priorityEscalation()'s own delegation chain, and must not be touched by this extraction.

Because self::FLAG_ESCALATE (2) is a non-zero literal and therefore always truthy, the effective return contract is: true whenever $this->flags is any non-zero value (i.e., true if ANY of FLAG_ACTIVE=1, FLAG_ESCALATE=2, FLAG_NOALERTS=4, or FLAG_TRANSIENT=8 is set, not specifically FLAG_ESCALATE), and false only when $this->flags === 0. This diverges from the intended per-bit contract (truthy only when the FLAG_ESCALATE bit specifically is set) that is correctly implemented elsewhere in the same class (getInfo()'s enable_priority_escalation key, hasFlag()).
